sources.title: NGSS 4-ESS3-1: Obtain and combine information to describe that energy and fuels are derived from natural resources and their uses affect the environment
U.S. Energy Information Administration, Energy Kids: Energy sources
U.S. Energy Information Administration, Energy Kids: Nonrenewable energy sources

steps.title: Two kinds
steps.instruction: Draw the line splitting the page in two.

note.text: All our energy comes from natural resources. Some are renewable, and some are nonrenewable.
Solar energy comes from sunlight. It's renewable: it's replaced naturally, so it won't run out.
Solar panels change sunlight into electricity.

steps.title: Wind turbine
steps.instruction: Trace the turbine's pole and hub.

note.text: Wind is renewable too. Wind turbines turn moving air into electricity.
The wind keeps blowing, so this energy source is replaced naturally.

steps.title: Moving water
steps.instruction: Draw the two waves of moving water.

note.text: Hydropower uses moving water to make electricity. It's renewable too: most renewable energy is used to make electricity.
Coal is a fossil fuel. It took thousands of years to form from buried plants and animals. It's nonrenewable.
note.remember: Fossil fuels: coal, oil, natural gas.

note.text: Oil is a fossil fuel too. We can only use what's already in the ground, so one day it could run out.

steps.title: Barrel bands
steps.instruction: Draw the two bands around the barrel.

note.text: Crude oil is also called petroleum.

steps.title: Natural gas
steps.instruction: Trace the flame of natural gas.

note.text: Natural gas is the third fossil fuel. Like coal and oil, it can't be made again quickly.

steps.title: Explain
steps.question: Why are coal, oil and natural gas called nonrenewable?

options.text: They took a very long time to form, so we can't make more quickly
options.feedback: Yes. They formed from buried plants and animals long ago. There's only so much in the ground.
Weight isn't it. They can't be made again in a short time.
They make lots of energy, but they can't be replaced quickly.
It's about supply: they can't be made again quickly.

steps.title: Sort it
steps.question: Which of these is a renewable energy source?

options.feedback: Right. The wind is replaced naturally, so it won't run out.
Coal is a fossil fuel: nonrenewable.
Natural gas is a fossil fuel: nonrenewable.
Uranium, used in nuclear power, is mined and is nonrenewable.
